result.process_summary: Both the nesting‑doll scenario and recursion involve repeatedly applying the same operation to a smaller instance of the same structure until a minimal, non‑divisible case is reached (the base case), then reversing the process to combine the results back up to the original level.
potential_breaks: The analogy depicts a strictly linear chain of dolls, which aligns with simple (single‑branch) recursion but does not capture branching recursion where a call may spawn multiple subcalls.
Physical dolls are static objects; opening and closing them is a one‑time action, whereas recursive calls are dynamic and can involve varying amounts of computation.
The analogy suggests a deterministic order of unwinding, whereas actual recursion may involve early returns or tail‑call optimizations that differ from the literal re‑assembly of dolls.
